title: In vivo assessment of S. scimitus predation upon bee brood
author: Sabrina Rondeau
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.unaevae

steps.title: Assign hives to treatments
steps.instruction: Randomly assign each hive to either the control or treated group and clearly label each hive.

steps.title: Set up queen exclusion cage
steps.instruction: For each colony, place an empty comb with worker cells inside an exclusion cage together with the queen, position the cage in the brood chamber, allow the queen to lay eggs for 48 h, then remove the queen, re‑introduce her to the colony, quickly mark every egg‑containing cell on both sides of the frame using a permanent marker and a transparent acetate sheet, and finally return the frame to the exclusion cage and place the cage back in the middle of the brood chamber to prevent further oviposition.

substeps.instruction: Place empty comb with worker cells in exclusion cage with queen.
Insert cage into brood chamber and let queen lay eggs for 48 h.
Remove queen from cage and return her to the colony.
Mark position of each egg‑containing cell on both sides of the frame with permanent marker and acetate sheet (work quickly to avoid egg drying).
Return frame to exclusion cage and reposition cage in middle of brood chamber.

steps.title: Apply biocontrol or control material
steps.instruction: Pour the designated amount (500 ml in this experiment) of the commercial biocontrol product containing Stratiolaelaps scimitus for the treated group, or the same volume of pre‑autoclaved vermiculite for the control group, onto the queen excluder, pouring parallel to the brood frames so the material is partially retained by the excluder and the top of the frames.

steps.title: Monitor mite presence visually
steps.instruction: At each brood‑monitoring period, visually inspect the hive floor and frames to confirm that predatory mites remain in the hive; observing five to ten mites during an inspection is considered satisfactory.

steps.title: Collect debris sample at trial end
steps.instruction: When the trial concludes, collect a sample of debris from the bottom of the hive for later screening and identification of mites under a stereomicroscope.

steps.title: Count brood survival on acetate
steps.instruction: During each brood‑monitoring period, use the acetate sheets to count the number of cells containing brood and calculate the percentage of eggs and larvae that survived to cell capping.
